newsitem.title: UK: NatWest cites competition for Xmas working.
newsitem.headline: NatWest cites competition for Xmas working.

text.p: National Westminster Bak Plc said on Monday its decision to open its branches later on Christmas Eve stemmed from the fact that its competitors were staying open later and its customers wanted the branches to be open.
Earlier, banking, insurance and finance trade union BIFU said it would ballot members at NatWest and Lloyds TSB, asking them to back a half-day strike to force closure of branches.
It said it had reached agreements with Barclays and Midland Bank, a unit of HSBC Holdings on compensation for staff expected to work later on Christmas Eve.
English banks have traditionally closed early on Christmas Eve but this year, Lloyds TSB wants to close at 1630 GMT, while NatWest will close its doors at 1530 GMT.

A spokesman for NatWest said that since agreeing with the union that branches would close at lunch-time on December 24, it had recorded considerable customer demand for its branches to remain open. Also, it had noted its competitors planned to close later.
The spokesman said it was offering a day's extra leave for those having to work after 1300 GMT on Christmas Eve, which was more than the other banks.
A spokeswoman for Lloyds TSB confirmed that its decision to open later was based on changing competitive pressures.
"Times have changed and we think our staff will understand that we are in a highly competitive industry now and that we have to be open when our customers want us," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
A BIFU spokesman rejected the banks' claim that there was customer demand for longer hours on Christmas Eve and accused the banks of acting like sheep.
"There's no evidence of customer demand," said the BIFU spokesman.
